title: The Fox and the Hedgehog

full_text:
A fox, attempting to leap across a swollen mountain torrent, was swept downstream by the rushing current and cast battered and bruised into a muddy bog. Trapped in the deep mire, unable to pull his paws free, he lay helpless while swarms of bloodthirsty horseflies settled upon his skin, stinging him mercilessly and drinking their fill.

A kindly hedgehog, bustling past through the sedges, was touched with pity at the sight of the suffering animal.

"Neighbor Fox," whispered the hedgehog, stepping toward the mire, "you are in torment! Shall I use my prickles to drive off these vicious flies that are draining your life away?"

"No, I beg you, do not touch them!" gasped the fox weakly through gritted teeth.

The hedgehog stared in surprise: "Why on earth would you wish to keep these tormentors on your back?"

"Because," explained the wise fox with a painful groan, "these flies upon me are already bloated and gorged with my blood; their stings have grown dull, and they can drink no more. If you drive them away, a fresh swarm of starving, ravenous flies will take their place and drain every remaining drop of blood from my veins!"
moral: Better to endure familiar burdens than invite fresh and hungrier afflictions.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Fox and the Hedgehog"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
